title: Symplectic Fillings And Convexity
notes: Open with the boundary-interface question. Up to this point the class has treated contact manifolds mostly intrinsically; this chapter asks when the same manifold can be read as the boundary of a symplectic world. The picture should make orientation and transversality visible before the definitions split into weak, dominating, and strong forms.

title: Filling Taxonomy
notes: Separate the three adjectives carefully because they encode different amounts of boundary control. Weak filling is only a positivity condition on the contact hyperplanes. Domination fixes the conformal symplectic class on those hyperplanes. Strong filling adds an outward Liouville field, which is the data that later makes collars and gluing behave cleanly.

title: Strong Collar Model
notes: Use the collar as the operational meaning of strong filling. Near the boundary the Liouville flow supplies a coordinate t and the symplectic form is the exact model d of e to the t times alpha. The arrow points outward at t equals zero; reversing that arrow would change convexity into concavity.

title: Dimension Split
notes: The theorem is a small implication graph with a dimension-dependent hinge. In dimension three, weak positivity and domination coincide because the contact plane is two dimensional and all positive area forms differ by a positive function. In higher dimensions, domination and strong filling coincide, while weak filling remains genuinely broader.

title: Domination To Strong
notes: Sketch the proof move, not every calculation. Domination lets us choose alpha so that omega and d alpha agree on xi. The higher-dimensional wedge argument forces the extra beta term to vanish on the boundary, yielding omega restricted to T M equals d alpha. Then the lemma supplies the Liouville vector field.

title: Weak And Orientation Tests
notes: Read the local check record as a boundary diagnostic. The strong collar has exactness, transversality, and positivity at once. A weak filling preserves positivity without an exact Liouville collar. The wrong-orientation model warns that an exact collar with a transverse vector field is still not the desired filling if the induced boundary orientation is wrong.

title: Convex And Concave At Once
notes: This slide prevents a common intuition trap. Symplectic convexity is not ordinary visual bulging: the same unit circle in the plane can be made convex or concave by choosing different Liouville fields near it. What matters is the contact-type behavior of the vector field relative to the oriented boundary.

title: Cobordism Direction
notes: A symplectic cobordism is a directed transition between contact manifolds. The positive boundary is convex because the Liouville vector points outward there; the negative boundary is concave because it points inward there. A strong filling is the special case with no negative boundary, so the empty set feeds into M.

title: Gluing Cobordisms
notes: Explain gluing as collar bookkeeping. The two contact forms on the shared boundary define the same cooriented contact structure, so they differ by a positive conformal factor. The bridge region interpolates in the symplectization direction, and the form d of e to the t times alpha minus keeps the glued manifold symplectic.

title: Real Convexity Baseline
notes: Before entering complex tangencies, recall the real template. A defining function rho marks the region by rho less than zero and identifies the tangent hyperplane by d rho equals zero. Convexity is detected by the Hessian along tangent directions. The Levi form keeps this second-derivative spirit but discards the non-holomorphic part.

title: Complex Tangencies And Levi Form
notes: Introduce the complex tangent space as the largest J invariant part of the real tangent hyperplane. The Levi form is the Hermitian second derivative restricted to those complex tangencies. Strict positivity of this form is the complex-analytic analogue that will produce a contact structure on the boundary.

title: Levi Positivity To Contact
notes: Connect the analytic definition to contact topology. The one-form alpha equals minus d rho composed with J, so its kernel on the boundary is exactly the complex tangent distribution. The identity d alpha of X and J X equals four times the Levi form turns strict Levi positivity into a symplectic form on xi.

title: Unit Ball Calibration
notes: Use the unit ball as a calibration example. Its defining function has positive Levi eigenvalues, and the local check records this positive model. The complex tangencies on the sphere therefore form the standard contact structure. The example also shows why the complex boundary story is a filling story, not just a curvature computation.

title: Stein And Holomorphic Fillings
notes: Close the construction chain in two steps. Stein regular sublevels give strong fillings because the gradient of rho points outward and contraction with the Kahler form gives the boundary contact form. A holomorphic filling is a strictly Levi pseudoconvex boundary with xi equal to the complex tangent distribution and the correct boundary orientation; in dimension three the source theorem routes it to strong fillability through Stein filling and Gray stability.

title: Recap Exercise
notes: End with a classification habit rather than another theorem. Ask students to label which hypothesis is being used in each implication, failure, or construction. The point is to recognize whether a future argument needs mere positivity, conformal boundary control, an exact Liouville collar, or the complex-analytic route through Levi and Stein geometry.
